_internalReasoning: Extracted 42 visible menu items via OCR and categorized them into strict nutritional tiers based on preparation method (grilled/boiled vs fried/saucy).
summary: This menu analysis categorizes 42 dishes into 4 distinct health tiers. Grilled fish and clear preparations represent the safest choices, whereas heavy fried rice, seblak, and fried seafood present high sodium and saturated fat risks.

groups.groupName: Tier 1 - Safest Choice: Grilled Whole Fish & Rice
groups.comparisonSentence: This grilled fish group provides high-quality lean protein and omega-3 fatty acids with substantially lower saturated fat and sodium compared to the fried options.
groups.message: Grilled whole fish preparations offer an excellent nutritional profile, delivering high-quality protein and essential omega-3 fatty acids without the heavy burden of deep-frying oils. These dishes support cardiovascular and metabolic health when consumed with moderate portions of white or brown rice.
groups.orderingTip: Opt for grilled fish with minimal sweet soy glaze and request sambal on the side to control sodium intake.

groups.groupName: Tier 2 - Moderate Choice: Grilled Poultry Dishes
groups.comparisonSentence: Compared to simple grilled fish, grilled poultry offers comparable protein but slightly higher sodium and surface oils from marinades.
groups.message: Grilled chicken dishes provide a reliable source of lean poultry protein. However, sweet marinades and accompanying chili pastes can introduce moderate levels of added sugars and sodium. Ensure balanced vegetable intake alongside these items.
groups.orderingTip: Request chicken skin to be removed if managing lipid profiles, and limit sweet marinade residues.

groups.groupName: Tier 3 - Caution: Fried Fish & Sweet-Sour Dishes
groups.comparisonSentence: Unlike clean grilled proteins, these fried and sweet-sour dishes carry significantly higher caloric loads and oxidized cooking fats.
groups.message: Deep-frying and heavy sweet-and-sour sauces substantially increase the caloric density, saturated fat, and sugar content of these meals. Regular consumption may negatively impact lipid panels and glycemic control.
groups.orderingTip: Ask for sweet-sour sauces served in a separate bowl so you can moderate the sugar intake.

groups.groupName: Tier 4 - Alert: Fried Rice, Seblak & Spicy Noodles
groups.comparisonSentence: Representing the highest metabolic load on this menu, these fried rice, seblak, and noodle dishes combine refined carbohydrates with heavy oils and soaring sodium levels.
groups.message: Dishes like Nasi Goreng, Seblak, and Mie Tek-Tek are ultra-processed or oil-saturated carbohydrate bombs. They deliver very high sodium counts and refined starches that can provoke rapid glycemic spikes and long-term cardiovascular strain.
groups.orderingTip: Share these portions with a dining companion or pair with an abundant side of fresh raw vegetables to buffer glycemic impact.
